Continue forward beside the holder, level the right gripper for an upright side grasp.

Reduce the rejected approach further and gently move away from the near-singular wrist alignment.
Advance the open right fingers toward the holder side at mid-body height; preserve orientation and observe before closing.
Finish aligning the right finger gap around the holder body, keeping the holder upright and the left arm clear.

Continue lifting and turning the open right gripper toward a downward recovery approach over the holder.
Move above the fallen holder with the open right gripper and finish turning downward, retaining the current elbow-up branch.
Stop the interrupted rotation; retain the current downward-oblique grasp orientation and lower toward the holder body with small translations.

Test the closed holder grasp by lifting and drawing it back slightly, watching for the holder to follow rather than trusting gripper state.
The empty closed fingers show the holder was not retained. Reopen and shift farther right over its visible body before descending again.
Close the now-bracketing fingers, pause for closure, and lift the holder gently to verify retention visually.
The closed jaws are empty and above the holder. Reopen and descend more deeply around the visible body, with a small inward correction.
Use the head view to center the fingers farther inward and forward over the holder body, then close and make a small retention test.
The holder is still outside the grasp. Reopen and use the wrist view to shift the gap toward the visible holder, without another blind closure.
The forward approach reached an IK boundary. Retract and lift slightly while changing the approach heading, keeping the same elbow-up branch.
Angle the fingers farther forward toward the fallen holder while lowering the wrist, avoiding further extension of the arm.
Make a small pure lateral correction and check its effect in the wrist view before attempting closure.
The lateral correction brought the holder toward the gap. Continue centering and approach its body rather than closing below the base.
The holder body now lies between the fingers in the wrist view. Center slightly, close, and make a short lift to check retention.
The holder appears bracketed and follows the short lift. Keep the grip closed, retract from the reach limit, and start rotating its open end upward.
The holder remained on the table after lifting. Reopen and return with the pinch point shifted inward and behind the previous failed grasp.
Center the actual pinch region over the holder's middle and descend around its sidewalls, using a shallow, slow approach.
Advance the pinch region just past the holder base, close fully, pause, and test with a small vertical lift.
The jaws closed behind the holder rather than around it. Reopen and reposition toward its body, raising slightly to clear the table.
The holder now overlaps the actual closing region. Close with a longer stationary pause, then lift only two centimeters to check whether it follows.
The fingers are closing above the holder. Reopen and lower the actual pinch point to the sidewall height, with an inward correction.
Advance the open gap from the holder's end toward its middle using the wrist view, maintaining sidewall height.
Close around the sidewall now overlapping the pinch region, allow closure to settle, then test retention with a short lift.
The empty closed jaws are still behind the holder. Reopen, return to sidewall height, and advance farther around the body rather than its corner.
Forward reach was interrupted. Retract the wrist while flattening the approach and centering laterally on the holder, preserving the elbow-up branch.
No motion executed in the rejected chunk. Halve the retraction and orientation increments to leave the reach boundary continuously.
Advance the open fingers along their approach direction to put the holder sidewalls deeper into the closing region, then close while stationary.
Let closure settle, then lift and retract slightly without rotation to distinguish a retained holder from another empty grasp.
Correct the remaining lateral offset at the holder's near sidewall, lower to its mid-height, and close without lifting yet.
The gap is still below the holder in the wrist view. Reopen and test a pure upward correction to identify the required grasp height.

Change to a shallower side approach while lowering the open fingers toward the holder, using the wrist image to align the body with the closing region.
Lower the shallow side approach until the holder's near end is centered between the fingers; keep the gap fully open while aligning.
Center the near end laterally in the shallow side pinch, close fully with a pause, and make a small lift to check retention.
The holder is visually centered but still beyond the fingertips. Advance the open gripper along its approach axis before closing.
Advance a final short distance into the centered holder sidewalls, then close and pause before testing retention.
The advance stopped at the reach boundary before closure. Close at the current pose, then retract only slightly to test retention and regain reach margin.

The holder lies lengthwise across the jaws. Withdraw with the gripper open and change the approach to pinch across its narrower dimension.
Translate the newly oriented open pinch toward the holder's near end, using the head view to compensate for the changed fingertip offset.
The new approach hit the reach guard. Retract slightly and make the approach shallower while shifting inward, retaining the elbow-up branch.
The previous chunk executed nothing. Halve each increment to change the approach without a joint-target jump.
Use the changed wrist view to shift the gap inward and upward toward the holder, without further forward extension.
With the lateral alignment corrected, lower and advance the open pinch toward the holder's near sidewalls, then close at the approach endpoint.
Retract from the reach boundary and make the pinch shallower while keeping the holder in view; previous closure did not retain it.

Continue the shallower approach and a small inward centering correction, keeping the fingers open and recovering reach margin.
The holder is centered in the open gap; move the fingers deeper toward its near sidewalls at a shallow downward angle.
Lower the shallow fingers from above the holder to its sidewall height, then close while stationary; verify retention before any transport.
The fingers now appear to contact opposite sidewalls. Keep closed and lift with a small retraction to verify the holder follows.

At sidewall height, advance the open pinch toward the near end of the holder. Keep a slight upward clearance from the tabletop.

Make a small centering correction at the near end, close, and draw back at low height to regain reach margin if the sidewalls are retained.

Allow the centered sidewall closure to settle, then draw the holder back slowly with minimal lift to test retention and recover reach margin.

Center the near end in the forward-facing open gap and advance at constant height to get the fingers around, not merely against, its sidewalls.

Let closure finish, then gently retract and lift the near end with a small upward rotation. Check visually whether the holder follows.

At the lower height, reopen and advance slowly past the near face so the fingers can enclose the holder rather than press against its end.
The holder's long axis spans the jaw opening. Retract from the reach boundary and roll the open gripper to pinch across its narrower cross-section.
Finish orienting the jaw closure across the holder's narrow dimension while correcting the lateral offset. Keep the open fingers clear of the table.
The rolled jaw opening now spans the holder's narrow cross-section. Lower slowly to center that cross-section between the fingers, watching table clearance.
